en: Jupiter is so large that about 1,300 Earths could fit inside its massive volume.
The Moon is currently drifting away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year.
The closest star to Earth, Proxima Centauri, is located approximately 4.24 light-years away from our solar system.
On the Mohs hardness scale, talc is the softest mineral at level one, while diamond is the hardest at level ten.
The largest earthquake ever recorded happened in Chile in 1960, measuring a massive 9.5 on the magnitude scale.
About 97 percent of all water on Earth is salty ocean water, leaving only three percent as fresh water.
Earth's average global temperature has increased by about 1.1 degrees Celsius since the late 19th century.
A single handful of healthy soil can contain billions of microscopic bacteria, fungi, and other tiny living organisms.
Earth travels around the Sun at an average speed of about 107,000 kilometers per hour.
The Sun contains about 99.86 percent of all the mass in our entire solar system.
The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia was the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history.
Hurricane Patricia in 2015 produced the fastest recorded maximum sustained winds of 345 kilometers per hour.
